subject: general
question:
If θ is an acute angle, find the denominator D when

(cot θ - cosec θ)² = (1 - cos θ)/(D)
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Simplify the expression using the identity **(cosec θ − cot θ) = tan(θ/2)**. Given **(cot θ − cosec θ)²** is the same as **(cosec θ − cot θ)²**. We know **(1 − cos θ) / (1 + cos θ) = tan²(θ/2)**. Comparing **(1 − cos θ) / D = (1 − cos θ) / (1 + cos θ)**. **∴ The correct answer is 1 + cos θ.**
